overview: The file consists of two U.S. Department of State lists of papers indexing correspondence and cross-references concerning electric-power development in Taiwan (Formosa) in 1930–1931. Its principal subject is the proposed resumption, financing, and completion of the Sun Moon Lake hydroelectric project, then called the Lake Candidius or Lake Jitsugetsutan project. The entries record support from the Governor-General, plans to seek foreign and American loans, the Taiwan Power Company’s bond financing, possible construction and machinery contracts, and concern over whether political resignations in the colonial administration might affect the project.

subfiles.title: List of papers on resuming the Lake Candidius hydroelectric project
subfiles.about: An index sheet summarizes correspondence about reviving the Lake Candidius hydroelectric project and identifying firms able to undertake construction and supply equipment.
subfiles.summary: A Taihoku telegram reported indications that the Lake Candidius project would resume within a few months, with the Governor-General intending to seek approval in Tokyo. The plan contemplated raising 40 million yen through foreign loans and completing the project within three years. Subsequent Commerce Department correspondence requested the names and addresses of parties positioned to obtain construction, machinery, and supply contracts, and Taihoku was instructed to investigate.

subfiles.title: List of papers and cross-references on Taiwan Power Company financing
subfiles.about: An index sheet lists reports and cross-references concerning the Taiwan Power Company loan, the Sun Moon Lake project, colonial political changes, and American bond financing.
subfiles.summary: The sheet records a report from Reed at Taihoku that the Cabinet had approved a Taiwan Power Company loan and refers to a detailed report on the Lake Jitsugetsutan, or Lake Candidius, hydroelectric project. Another entry states that the resignation of the Governor-General of Formosa and most executive-department heads was not expected to affect the project. It also cross-references correspondence from J.P. Morgan & Co. about a proposed $22.8 million issue of forty-year, 5½-percent sinking-fund gold bonds, and records a Franklin telegram concerning a roughly $22.5 million American loan and plans to borrow 20 million yen from the Finance Department in Tokyo to repurchase bonds held in Japan.

interest: These sheets offer a compact roadmap to a larger body of diplomatic and commercial reporting on one of colonial Taiwan’s most important infrastructure projects. They are especially useful for tracing the intersection of Japanese colonial administration, American financial participation, and international competition for construction and equipment contracts. The variant names Lake Candidius and Lake Jitsugetsutan also help researchers connect English-language diplomatic records with sources concerning modern Sun Moon Lake.
